related_questions.question: What is required to reenter the U.S. from Canada?

text_blocks.snippet: To re-enter the U.S. from Canada, U.S. citizens generally need a valid U.S. passport or other approved travel document. Canadian citizens typically need a valid passport, and depending on their visa status, potentially an I-20 or DS-2019 form with a valid travel signature.
snippet_highlighted_words: a valid U.S. passport or other approved travel document

list.title: Passport:
list.snippet: A valid U.S. passport book or a passport card is generally required for air travel.

list.title: Other Approved Documents:
list.snippet: U.S. citizens may also be able to use other approved travel documents, such as those issued under the Western Hemisphere Travel Initiative (WHTI), according to the U.S. Department of State.

list.title: Passport:
list.snippet: Canadian citizens need a valid passport when entering the U.S., even when traveling by land or sea.

list.title: I-20 or DS-2019:
list.snippet: If you are a student on an F-1 or J-1 visa, you need your valid I-20 or DS-2019 form, respectively, with a travel signature from your Designated School Official (DSO) or Responsible Officer (RO), according to UC Santa Barbara.

list.title: Visa:
list.snippet: Canadian citizens generally don't need a visa to enter the U.S. for tourism or business, but there are exceptions.

list.title: Expiration Dates:
list.snippet: Ensure your passport and other required documents are valid and won't expire during your trip.

list.title: I-94:
list.snippet: Canadian citizens may need to obtain an I-94 form upon arrival, which indicates their authorized period of stay.

list.title: Financial Documents:
list.snippet: Students on F-1 or J-1 visas may need to show proof of sufficient financial resources.

list.title: Travel Signature:
list.snippet: For students on F-1 or J-1 visas, the travel signature on the I-20 or DS-2019 must be recent (typically within the last year, but potentially within the last 6 months for OPT/STEM OPT).

list.title: Visa Waiver Program:
list.snippet: If you are not a Canadian citizen, you may need a visa or ESTA (Electronic System for Travel Authorization) to enter the U.S., depending on your nationality.
